# Flossie Tulk

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen or eighteen  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c25 P61](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0061), [v1 c26 P4](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0004)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c11 P25](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0025)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c17 P37](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0037), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020)</sub>

## Appearance

Flossie is a heavy-set girl who attends school in Brierley. She wears puffed sleeves like the other girls in her class.

_Sources: [v1 c11 P29](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0029), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Personality

Flossie is moody, spiteful, and prone to harboring animosity when she does not get her way. She takes pleasure in the misfortune or embarrassment of others and frequently makes snide or critical remarks. She is also competitive and arrogant about her accomplishments, though she can be driven to dishonesty or malice. Despite her moody nature, she is capable of showing occasional politeness or regret after causing harm.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)_

- Moody  <sub>[v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)</sub>
- Spiteful  <sub>[v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047)</sub>
- Arrogant  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c25 P14](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0014)</sub>

## Abilities

- Skillful at walking wooden fences  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006)</sub>
- Knitting lace  <sub>[v1 c23 P25](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0025)</sub>

## Goals

- To lead her class academically  <sub>[v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025)</sub>
- To attend college simply to gain an education  <sub>[v1 c25 P14](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0014)</sub>

## History

Flossie attended Brierley school, where she frequently competed with Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow. She was caught peeking at her book during a spelling class by Nell, earning an icy look that made her blush. When Nell was punished by Mr. Pidgeon, Flossie grinned spitefully at her. She later participated in a game of 'daring' in the Pembroke garden, successfully walking the ridge of a wooden fence, and challenged Nell to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof, which led to Nell falling and spraining her ankle. Flossie was greatly relieved when Nell survived the fall. She joined the Regent's entrance class under Miss Thorne, though she disliked the bi-weekly recitation afternoons because she lacked creative imagination. She passed her entrance exams with a narrow three-point margin and attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow. While at Regent's, she shared a boarding house with Frank Stockley and was known for her caustic tongue, though she remained on speaking terms with her classmates. She later took the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics during her Sophomore year at Wexcombe.

> I don’t believe anyone could walk a ridgepole. At any rate, you couldn’t.  <sub>[v1 c23 P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)</sub>

> I’m really happy you made the trip up. I imagine you’re missing home—certain folks possess so little restraint regarding that.  <sub>[v1 c34 P18](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0018)</sub>

> That new dress of yours suits you quite well, Nell. Truthfully, it makes you look nearly pretty.  <sub>[v1 c25 P2](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0002)</sub>

> I am going to take the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics. I could win the one in Greek without difficulty, but I prefer to win the mathematical one since I wish to demonstrate to Ezra that I am truly remarkably brilliant.  <sub>[v1 c26 P3](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0003)</sub>
